lkm.title: Check known vulnerabilities?
lkm.p1: Meridian can look up every software version it finds (for example vsftpd 2.3.4) in the Vulners database and show known CVEs, public exploits and what to do about them. It applies to the next scan only, and you are asked again every time.
lkm.p2: This sends only software names and versions to vulners.com, never IP addresses or hostnames, and the nmap script also downloads fingerprint data from GitHub. Results are based on the version text, so some may not apply to patched systems.
lkm.demo: This is the demo: it uses sample data and sends nothing anywhere.

cli.help:
Meridian {version} - network scanner UI on top of nmap

Usage: meridian [option]
  (no option)      open the app window
  --serve          run without a window and print the URL to open yourself
  --lang CODE      language of the app and of this text ({langs}; default: your system language)
  --doctor         check this computer (Python, nmap, privileges, browser, folders) and say how to fix problems
  --version, -V    print the version and exit
  --uninstall      remove the app AND your saved data
                   (--keep-data keeps the data, --yes skips the question)
  --help, -h       show this help

Environment: MERIDIAN_PORT=8765 (preferred port; any free port is used if it is busy)
             MERIDIAN_LANG=en (same as --lang), MERIDIAN_NMAP=/path/to/nmap, MERIDIAN_DATA_DIR=/folder/for/saved/data
Scan only networks you own or have permission to test.
